title: College Football Playoff leaves open possibility that Rose Bowl will be played in primetime
content:
Almost half of the next edition of the College Football Playoff will air on TNT, and the Rose Bowl might be an evening kickoff for the first time in two decades.

The CFP on Monday revealed broadcast information and kickoff times for most of the 12-team tournament, which changes in 2026 with a new six-year media rights deal kicking in, though specifics of the quarterfinals are yet to be determined.

Notably, two first-round games, two quarterfinals and one semifinal will air on TNT, truTV and HBO Max as part of an expanded licensing deal after ESPN sold those game rights to Warner Bros. Discovery. Previously, TNT aired only two first-round games in the first two years of the 12-team Playoff.

ESPN will air a first-round game the night of Friday, Dec. 18, then another at noon ET the next day (with an ABC simulcast). TNT will take over the 3:30 p.m. ET and 7:30 p.m. ET games once again, with those two airing at the same time as NFL games.

For the quarterfinals, TNT will air the Fiesta Bowl on the night of Dec. 30 — the game is not on New Year’s Eve because the NFL has a Thursday night game. TNT will also air either the Cotton Bowl or Sugar Bowl at noon ET on New Year’s Day. ESPN will hold the 4 p.m. ET and 8 p.m. ET slots, one of which will be the Rose Bowl.

A CFP spokesperson confirmed it’s possible the Rose Bowl could end up in the 8 p.m. slot (5 p.m. local), to be determined at a later date. If it happens, it would be the first time the Rose Bowl kicks off that late since the Texas-USC national championship to cap the 2005 season. (BCS championship games in 2009 and 2013 were at the Rose Bowl Stadium but were separate from the Rose Bowl Game.)

The Rose Bowl already established it preferred to remain on New Year’s Day and not serve as a CFP semifinal later in January, which is why the Fiesta Bowl served as a semifinal for the last two years. The Rose Bowl also moved up its kickoff by one hour last season, so the Sugar Bowl could start at an earlier time, which impacted the timing of the traditional game sunset. Neither the Fiesta Bowl nor the Rose Bowl will take the noon ET slot on New Year’s Day under this new deal, due to time zones.

Next year’s national championship game will air on both ESPN and ABC for the first time in the CFP era. It’ll take place on Jan. 25, a week later than the past two seasons. That’s a result of New Year’s Day falling on a Friday, which pushes the Thursday/Friday semifinals out almost two weeks past New Year’s, in order to avoid one team playing on six days’ rest. That in turn pushed the national title game to late January.
